entry.title: Mend for Bitbucket DC: Version 26.4.1.1 (19-April-2026)
entry.content:
Unified Agent 26.3.2 | Renovate 43.102.11 | Remediate 26.4.1 | Pre-Scan Builder (PSB) 25.8.1

New Features and Updates

  • Added support for disabling specific package manager resolvers using the {PACAKGE_MANAGER}.resolveDependencies parameter, allowing more granular control over dependency resolution.

Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where the clone, fetch, and checkout commands in the scanner were limited to a fixed 15‑minute timeout, which caused failures with large repositories. Timeouts are now configurable through the environment variables listed below, providing better support for large repositories.

    • GIT_CLONE_TIMEOUT_MINS 

    • GIT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MINS 

    • GIT_CHECKOUT_TIMEOUT_MINS

entry.title: Mend for GitHub.com: Version 26.4.3 (17-May-2026)
entry.content:
Resolved Issues

  • (SCA) Fixed an issue where projects specifying .NET 10 in the .csproj file did not resolve dependencies as expected. The system now detects SDK version mismatches, automatically installs the required .NET SDK, and retries dependency resolution to ensure all dependencies are properly detected.

entry.title: Mend Developer Platform: Version 26.4.3 (17-May-2026)
entry.content:
New Features and Updates

  • Improved the navigation in the repository page within the developer platform, especially for organizations with a large number of repositories.

Resolved Issues

  • (AZDO) Fixed an issue where pull request scans between configured base branches in Azure DevOps could fail with a "Failed to retrieve base branch mend project" error, even though a valid scan occurred on the commit itself. This resolves inconsistent scan behavior when multiple base branches are configured.

  • (AZDO) Fixed an issue where onboarding failed for users with a large number of Azure DevOps organizations, causing excessive loading times and timeouts. The onboarding flow was redesigned to fetch and display organizations first, allowing users to select specific organizations before loading their projects, significantly improving performance and user experience.

  • (SCA) Fixed an issue where projects specifying .NET 10 in the .csproj file did not resolve dependencies as expected. The system now detects SDK version mismatches, automatically installs the required .NET SDK, and retries dependency resolution to ensure all dependencies are properly detected.

entry.title: Mend CLI: Version 26.4.3 (18-May-2026)
entry.content:
New Features and Updates

  • (Limited Availability) (SCA) Introducing an improved .NET resolver which relies on .deps.json in the build folder for increased dependency detection accuracy.

Resolved Issues

  • (SCA) Fixed an issue where dependency scans would intermittently fail during policy compliance checks, resulting in an "asyncCheckPolicyCompliace failed" message. Scans now complete successfully without unexpected interruptions.

  • (SCA) Fixed an issue where environment variable-based configurations were not loaded correctly in the CLI, resulting in empty values. The CLI now properly reads MEND_-prefixed environment variables and applies them as expected.

entry.title: Mend AI: Version 25.12.1 (05-January-2026)
entry.content:
New Features and Updates

  • (Premium / Core) Introducing System Prompt Risk (open beta), a new detection and remediation offering by Mend AI, for mitigating risks posed by system prompts used in conversational AI interfaces.

    • A new System Prompt Risk table inventories system prompts and provides quick export/sharing and deep-link side panel for prompt context.

    • System Prompt Risks are integrated into the existing AI Security Risk Factors across Projects and Applications. The classification appears as a Conversational Interface chip, is filterable, and automatically participates in dashboards and workflows.

    • Remediation in the form of a hardened system prompt is available in the System Prompt side panel, providing clear, copy-ready remediation guidance for AppSec engineers and developers.

    • The AI Security Dashboard has been enriched with system prompt risk data.

    • System prompt risk data is also available via API.

entry.title: Mend Container: Version 26.4.2 (03-May-2026)
entry.content:
Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where the bson package version was incorrectly detected as UNKNOWN, resulting in a false positive for CVE-2020-7610. The scanner now accurately identifies bson@1.1.4 and avoids reporting this vulnerability when the correct version is present.

entry.title: Mend SAST: Version 26.4.3 (18-May-2026)
entry.content:
New Features and Updates

  • Mend now offers a SAST plugin for JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ and others), allowing developers to find and fix security vulnerabilities without leaving their editor. The plugin allows developers to run a scan, highlights vulnerable lines of code directly in the editor, and separates the new issues introduced by the developer's own changes from the existing issues — keeping the noise low. For each finding, developers can see remediation suggestions, code flow traces, CWE descriptions, and training materials. Applying a fix is a single click: the plugin shows a code diff and patches the file automatically. IDE scans are kept isolated from the Mend AppSec Platform, meaning local scans don't affect project-level statistics.

  • The Gen 2 Go detection engine is now generally available, delivering increased coverage and accuracy for Go code analysis.

  • Secrets scanning now detects hardcoded Stripe credentials more robustly.

  • Improved secret detection by addressing cases where certain secrets were previously missed during scanning.

Resolved Issues

  • Fixed an issue where SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) vulnerabilities were incorrectly flagged as false positives in C# (Gen2) scans.

entry.title: Mend AppSec Platform: Version 26.4.3 (17-May-2026)
entry.content:
New Features and Updates

  • (Closed Beta) Introducing custom roles with granular permissions, allowing organizations to define and assign least-privilege access via groups at both organization and application levels. This update enhances security and governance by enabling fine-grained control, separation of duties, and centralized role management, while maintaining full compatibility with existing roles.

  • Mend's MCP server now exposes security findings across SAST and SCA scanning engines so developers can query vulnerability data directly from their AI-powered tools and workflows. The findings come enriched with remediation suggestions, making it easier to understand and fix issues without leaving the tools they already use, or by instructing an agent to fix them. Developers can ask questions like "What are the top 5 security issues in this repo?" or "Explain this SQL injection finding" and their preferred agent will be able to answer these questions by communicating with the MCP server.

  • UI Improvements:

    • Added an "Assigned by" field to each copyright entry in the OS library side panel, making it clear whether a copyright was detected by Mend.io or manually set by a user. This enhancement improves audit clarity by matching the display logic already used in the Licenses tab, helping users easily distinguish between system-detected and user-overridden copyrights.

    • Replaced the floating filter row in Admin > Applications with platform-standard filter buttons, saving vertical space and making active filters clearer. This update aligns the filtering experience with the rest of the platform for a more consistent and user-friendly interface.

Resolved Issues

  • (SCA) Fixed an issue where Mend CLI dependency scans would intermittently fail during policy compliance checks, resulting in an "asyncCheckPolicyCompliace failed" message. Scans now complete successfully without unexpected interruptions.
